intro: Things I want to build next. Mostly games right now, but anything cool is fair game.

ideas.name: Boot-sector game
ideas.pitch: A whole game in 512 bytes of x86 real-mode assembly that boots straight from the BIOS, no OS. Snake or a tiny shooter.
ideas.first_step: Get a 'hello' boot sector printing to the screen in QEMU.

ideas.name: Night Shift (hacking sim)
ideas.pitch: A browser hacking-sim where you pentest a fictional company: fake shell, fake network, real techniques (recon, creds, pivots) and a story told through the files you find.
ideas.first_step: Write the fictional network and one 15-minute mission on paper.

ideas.name: JavaShooter 2
ideas.pitch: Rebuild my roguelike shooter in Godot with procedural rooms, item synergies, bosses, controller support and a real release on itch.io.
ideas.first_step: Port the core movement + shooting loop and see if it feels better.

ideas.name: CHIP-8 emulator
ideas.pitch: The classic first emulator: 35 opcodes, a 64x32 screen, and suddenly you can play Pong and Space Invaders ROMs on code you wrote.
ideas.first_step: Implement the fetch/decode loop and get the IBM logo test ROM drawing.

ideas.name: Game Boy emulator
ideas.pitch: The step up from CHIP-8: emulate the Sharp LR35902 CPU, the PPU and the memory bank controllers well enough to boot Tetris.
ideas.first_step: Pass Blargg's cpu_instrs test ROMs.

ideas.name: Terminal roguelike
ideas.pitch: An ASCII dungeon crawler that runs in a real terminal (and later inside ghost on 0xDay): field of view, permadeath, generated floors.
ideas.first_step: BSP dungeon generator + an @ that walks around.

ideas.name: LAN party game
ideas.pitch: A 4-player top-down arena game with a dedicated server running on my Proxmox box, so friends can join over Tailscale.
ideas.first_step: Two clients moving the same box over the network.

ideas.name: Rollback netcode lab
ideas.pitch: A tiny 2-player fighting game built only to learn rollback netcode: deterministic sim, input delay vs rollback, and a fake-latency slider.
ideas.first_step: Make the game loop fully deterministic and replayable from inputs.

ideas.name: Game jam entry
ideas.pitch: Ship something in 48 hours at Ludum Dare or the GMTK jam. Small scope, real deadline, real players.
ideas.first_step: Pick the next jam on itch.io and put it on the calendar.

ideas.name: Voxel engine
ideas.pitch: A block world from scratch: chunked terrain from noise, greedy meshing, frustum culling, and breaking/placing blocks.
ideas.first_step: Render one textured chunk with a fly camera.

ideas.name: Anti-cheat vs. cheat
ideas.pitch: Write a memory-scanner cheat for my own game, then write the anti-cheat that catches it. Game hacking meets reverse engineering, and it's all my own code.
ideas.first_step: Find the player health address in JavaShooter with Cheat Engine.

ideas.name: Speedrun autosplitter
ideas.pitch: A LiveSplit autosplitter that reads game memory to split runs automatically. Small, useful, and secretly a memory-forensics exercise.
ideas.first_step: Pick a game and find a stable pointer to the level ID.

ideas.name: Internet honeypot
ideas.pitch: Run T-Pot on a cheap VPS, ship the logs to my homelab SIEM, and publish a live 'who's knocking' dashboard on 0xDay.
ideas.first_step: Spin up T-Pot and leave it for 48 hours.

ideas.name: Malware sandbox pipeline
ideas.pitch: An isolated CAPE sandbox VLAN in Proxmox: drop a sample, get a report with API calls, network IOCs and a YARA hit list.
ideas.first_step: Build the isolated VLAN with no route out.

ideas.name: Infrastructure as code homelab
ideas.pitch: Rebuild all seven homelab VMs from Terraform + Ansible so the whole lab can be destroyed and recreated with one command.
ideas.first_step: Terraform one VM on Proxmox from a cloud-init template.

ideas.name: Pi k3s cluster
ideas.pitch: Three Raspberry Pis running k3s, hosting game servers and small services, with GitOps deploys and a little rack I build myself.
ideas.first_step: Get two nodes joined and one pod scheduled.

ideas.name: E-ink lab status board
ideas.pitch: An e-ink screen on the desk showing VM health, SIEM alert counts and TryHackMe streak, refreshed every few minutes.
ideas.first_step: Draw text on the panel from the ESP32.

ideas.name: Macro pad
ideas.pitch: A 3D-printed 9-key macro pad with a rotary encoder running QMK: one key per VM snapshot, one to open ghost, one to lock the screen.
ideas.first_step: Hand-wire 4 switches to a Pico and get keypresses.

ideas.name: DIY handheld
ideas.pitch: A pocket game console: Pi Zero 2 W, a small IPS screen, a custom PCB for the buttons, and my own games preloaded.
ideas.first_step: Breadboard the screen and buttons on a Pi Zero.

ideas.name: Wi-Fi attack detector
ideas.pitch: An ESP32 that watches my own network for deauth floods and evil-twin APs and pings an alert to the SIEM. Defensive only.
ideas.first_step: Put the ESP32 in promiscuous mode and count management frames.

ideas.name: Packet sonifier
ideas.pitch: Turn live network traffic into music: protocols are instruments, packet size is pitch. A port scan should sound terrible.
ideas.first_step: Map TCP/UDP/ICMP to three notes and listen to a pcap.

ideas.name: Local LLM log triage
ideas.pitch: A local model on the homelab that reads Security Onion alerts and writes a plain-English 'what happened' summary for each one.
ideas.first_step: Feed it 20 real alerts and grade the summaries.

ideas.name: ghost CLI
ideas.pitch: Port ghost, the site's terminal assistant, to a real command-line tool: `pip install ghost-0xday` and browse the blog from any shell.
ideas.first_step: Read data.js and print the post list.

ideas.name: Toy language + compiler
ideas.pitch: A small language with a lexer, parser, type checker and an x86-64 backend. Bonus: write a game in it.
ideas.first_step: Compile integer arithmetic to assembly that runs.

ideas.name: Hobby OS
ideas.pitch: Boot past the boot sector: protected mode, a keyboard driver, a framebuffer and a shell. Endgame is running the boot-sector game as a program.
ideas.first_step: Follow the OSDev bare bones tutorial to a kernel that prints.

ideas.name: Tiny CTF platform
ideas.pitch: Host a small CTF for friends or an LSU club: challenges I write from my labs (forensics, RE, web), scoreboard, hints.
ideas.first_step: Write three challenges from the HiTek and wg2 work.
